name: Gendle & McGrath 2012 replication: 8 Coil Shakti amygdala signal, both temporal lobes
origin: Mathew H. Gendle & Megan G. McGrath, Elon University (independent test); device, amygdala signal and coil set-up by Todd Murphy (8 Coil Shakti)
summary: A copy, for blinded self-tests, of the randomized, placebo-controlled test of a commercial God-Helmet-type device: one 30-min session of the 8 Coil Shakti 'amygdala signal' over both temporal lobes at up to 1 uT, with emotional ratings of 54 colour photographs. In 37 people the field changed neither the ratings nor how they depended on the pictures' valence.
notes: Original study: 37 people were randomized to one 30-min session of field or sham and rated their emotional reactions to 54 colour photographs of differing emotional valence; the ratings followed valence, but the field neither changed them nor interacted with valence. From Murphy's reply: the 'amygdala signal' over both temporal lobes; up to 1 uT, the default output, with no per-person adjustment and without the vendor's screening questionnaire; an onboard Realtek HD sound device; daytime sessions; mean Kp 1.03 (SD 0.76); pictures close to those of an earlier Italian study with International Affective Picture System images, minus the explicitly sexual or violent ones; and a consent form telling participants that '(1) slight muscle twitching, (2) minor headache, (3) unusual skin sensations, (4) odd smells, (5) the subjective sensation of fear or a "sensed presence" (i.e., someone in the room), or (6) subtle alterations in perception and/or emotional states' might occur. When in the session the pictures were rated, the rating scale, and who knew the condition are not in the available sources (the paper is closed access); per Murphy, no trait or mood questionnaires were given. Field: the 8 Coil Shakti standard temporal set-up, as in shakti-alternate: a 4-coil cross on each temporal lobe (site names an inference: FT7, C5, TP7, T9 and FT8, C6, TP8, T10); each stereo channel drives one + and one - coil on each side (C5, FT7, T10 and TP8 reversed, weight -1), and the signal switches between the top-bottom and the front-back pairs every 0.5 s. The vendor offers fast and slow alternation and a 'high-speed' amygdala signal; which the study used is not published, so the normal-speed signal with fast alternation (the vendor's 'most effective') is assumed. The amygdala file is proprietary and is approximated by the built-in accelerating burst (6 to 30 Hz), 230 points of 3 ms (0.69 s), one every 4.5 s so that the half-second clock and the signal repeat together. The field is the same as shakti-alternate; this file adds the study's procedure and fixes the session to the published 30 min. Murphy's objections are vendor claims: the bilateral amygdala signal is the weakest configuration; the 'feelgood' session (two signals with 4-s pauses over the frontal lobes, weekly for six weeks; murphy-shakti8-feelgood-1phase-frontal) would have tested the vendor's mood claim; daytime sessions, onboard sound and the warnings in the consent form worked against an effect. A popular review restated the result as 'no significant difference in emotional state' (Aaen-Stockdale 2012), but the study measured responses to pictures, not mood. With Granqvist 2005 this is one of the two independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields; neither found a field effect. How to run it with the app: tick Blind in Programs; the helmet's random generator picks real or sham each session and reveals it only after you save the rating (the original randomized between people, so a self-test compares your own real and sham sessions). The app has no picture task: prepare a fixed, valence-balanced set of 54 photographs (positive, neutral and negative) and rate your reaction to each on the same scale in every session, before saving the 0-10 rating; reactions fade with repeated viewing, so keep order and timing identical, or use parallel sets. Read the consent list above beforehand, as the participants did. The Log tab keeps condition, rating and Kp. Guides -> Enrollment battery is optional (the original used no trait measures); the Experiment tab runs psi trials and is not needed. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, a psychiatric condition or medication, or migraine; stop on fear or distress.
setting: By day, seated in an ordinary quiet room; no sensory deprivation is reported. A helper who does not know the condition can start the Blind session and present the photographs.
schedule: One 30-min session per person in the original. Self-test: a fixed number of Blind sessions decided in advance, at least 72 h apart (the vendor's spacing rule), each with the same picture procedure.
source: Gendle & McGrath 2012, Can the 8-coil Shakti alter subjective emotional experience?
